# Ramonyx — llms-full (public)

> Full public corpus for agents: public machine layer (JSON) + public documentation.
> Source: repo RamonyxJS/ramonyx (https://ramonyxjs.github.io/ramonyx). Internal docs are never included.

## docs/public/machine/rules.json

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "rules": [
    {
      "id": "erasable-syntax",
      "rule": "Tulis TypeScript yang erasable: dilarang `enum`, `namespace`, parameter property, dan `import =`. Tipe harus hilang saat transpile.",
      "rationale": "Paket framework diekspor sebagai `.ts` dan dijalankan Node type stripping (tanpa transpile). Sintaks non-erasable gagal saat runtime.",
      "scope": "framework",
      "good": "export type Status = \"ok\" | \"error\";\nconst STATUS = { ok: \"ok\" } as const;",
      "bad": "enum Status { Ok, Error }\nclass X { constructor(private y: number) {} }",
      "enforcement": "tsconfig `erasableSyntaxOnly` + `verbatimModuleSyntax`; `pnpm typecheck`",
      "adrs": ["ADR-0002", "ADR-0006"]
    },
    {
      "id": "relative-imports-extension",
      "rule": "Impor relatif memakai ekstensi eksplisit: `./x.ts` / `./x.tsx` (bukan `./x`).",
      "rationale": "Node ESM tidak menebak ekstensi; paket diekspor sebagai sumber `.ts` dan dijalankan langsung.",
      "scope": "framework",
      "good": "import { createApp } from \"./app.ts\";",
      "bad": "import { createApp } from \"./app\";",
      "enforcement": "Konsisten di seluruh repo; test loader akan gagal bila salah",
      "adrs": ["ADR-0002"]
    },
    {
      "id": "node-builtins-boundary",
      "rule": "Impor `node:*` hanya di paket Node-only (adapter-runtime, compiler, bundler, ssr, react, security, devtools, mcp-docs-server, plugin-image). Paket edge-safe (core, router, schema, server, testing, ramonyx) dilarang.",
      "rationale": "Paket edge-safe harus berjalan di runtime edge/serverless tanpa `node:*` (artefak `--target edge`, ADR-0058); paket Node-only memang butuh fs/net/build.",
      "scope": "framework",
      "good": "// packages/security/src/ssrf.ts\nimport { lookup } from \"node:dns/promises\";",
      "bad": "// packages/core/src/route.ts\nimport { readFile } from \"node:fs/promises\";",
      "enforcement": "Biome `noRestrictedImports` (packages/core|router|schema|server|testing|ramonyx) + guard build edge",
      "adrs": ["ADR-0002", "ADR-0015"]
    },
    {
      "id": "no-jsx-in-framework",
      "rule": "Paket framework tidak berisi JSX; JSX hanya di kode aplikasi (`.tsx`) yang dijalankan lewat loader dev/test.",
      "rationale": "Node type stripping tidak memproses JSX; paket framework harus berjalan di Node murni tanpa loader.",
      "scope": "framework",
      "good": "// packages/react/src/renderer.ts — fungsi murni tanpa JSX\nreturn createElement(page.component, props);",
      "bad": "// packages/react/src/renderer.ts\nreturn <page.component {...props} />;",
      "enforcement": "Struktur repo (tidak ada `.tsx` di packages/*/src) + test",
      "adrs": ["ADR-0006"]
    },
    {
      "id": "test-server-close-finally",
      "rule": "Setiap server yang dijalankan test WAJIB `close()` di blok `finally`.",
      "rationale": "Assert gagal sebelum `close()` membocorkan listener → `node --test` menggantung tanpa batas (pernah terjadi di CI).",
      "scope": "repo",
      "good": "const server = await start();\ntry { ...assert... } finally { await server.close(); }",
      "bad": "const server = await start();\nassert.equal(...); // gagal → server tidak pernah ditutup\nawait server.close();",
      "enforcement": "`--test-timeout=120000` + `--test-force-exit` sebagai jaring pengaman; konvensi review",
      "adrs": []
    },
    {
      "id": "node-env-production",
      "rule": "Produksi WAJIB `NODE_ENV=production` (skrip `start`/`docs`/bench dan template `create-app` sudah men-set).",
      "rationale": "Tanpa itu React berjalan build dev — pernah terjadi di server produksi (ADR-0048).",
      "scope": "app",
      "good": "\"start\": \"NODE_ENV=production node --import ./tools/register.mjs src/server.ts\"",
      "bad": "\"start\": \"node src/server.ts\"",
      "enforcement": "Template + skrip repo sudah benar; CI menjalankan build produksi di e2e",
      "adrs": ["ADR-0048"]
    },
    {
      "id": "loader-data-json",
      "rule": "Data loader halaman harus JSON-serializable.",
      "rationale": "Payload hydration ditanam inline ke HTML (`window.__RAMONYX__`); nilai non-JSON (function/class/Date) hilang atau error.",
      "scope": "app",
      "good": "export function load() { return { items: [\"a\", \"b\"] }; }",
```

```json
      "related": ["Hydration", "Streaming SSR"],

    },
    {
      "term": "Streaming SSR",

      "related": ["SSR (Server-Side Rendering)", "Suspense"],
      "docs": "docs/public/adr/0047-ssr-streaming.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Hydration",
      "definition": "Mengaktifkan React di browser atas HTML SSR: payload inline `window.__RAMONYX__` + satu bundle client + `hydrateRoot`. Halaman error tidak di-hydrate.",
      "related": ["SSR (Server-Side Rendering)", "Soft navigation"],
      "docs": "docs/public/adr/0007-hydration.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Soft navigation",
      "definition": "Navigasi klien tanpa full reload: fetch HTML halaman → swap `#ramonyx-root` → re-hydrate; `document.title` + scroll direset. Belum ada prefetch.",
      "related": ["Hydration"]
    },
    {
      "term": "Loader",

    },

    },

    },

    },
    {

    {

    },
    {
      "term": "Landlock",

      "related": ["Plugin (runtime)", "Deny-all"]
    },
    {
```

## docs/public/adr/0007-hydration.md

---
adr: 0007
title: "Hydration: inline payload + one client bundle"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0007: Hydration — Inline Payload + One Client Bundle

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-18

## Context

After server rendering, the client needs the same data the server used. A second data request after
load costs a round trip and can render a different result. Multiple per-page bundles multiply
requests and cache misses.

## Decision

1. Server rendering embeds a JSON payload in the document:
   `window.__RAMONYX__ = { path, params, data, action, locale }`.
2. The client is **one bundle** (hashed, immutable) that hydrates the current page from that payload
   and wires soft navigation.
3. The payload is JSON-serializable by contract; non-serializable data is a bug in the loader.
4. Error pages are **not** hydrated — they are server-only output.

## Consequences

- Hydration performs no extra data request.
- Loader data shapes the public contract: anything non-JSON must be transformed in the loader.
- The single bundle grows with the app; code splitting per route is a future optimization (not
  implemented).
- Soft navigation reuses the same payload shape, so server and client stay symmetric.

## docs/public/adr/0047-ssr-streaming.md

---
adr: 0047
title: "SSR streaming: opt-in, edge renderer, synchronous error pages"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0047: SSR Streaming — Opt-in, Edge Renderer

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-18

## Context

Large React trees benefit from streaming the shell before the whole page is ready. Streaming also
changes error semantics: once the first byte is sent, the HTTP status cannot change.

## Decision

1. Streaming is **opt-in** (`streaming: true` on page routes or `app.streaming` in config). The
   default remains synchronous rendering.
2. The React renderer uses `react-dom/server.edge` (`renderToReadableStream`) for both streaming and
   synchronous rendering, so Node and edge targets share one code path.
3. The document renderer is split around a body marker so custom HTML shells keep working; if the
   shell omits the marker, the synchronous path is used.
4. Error pages always render synchronously. Errors after the first streamed byte terminate the
   connection instead of changing the status.

## Consequences

- Apps choose the trade-off: faster TTFB and progressive paint vs. simpler error handling.
- `onRenderEnd` fires when the stream **starts** (not when it finishes) and reports
  `streaming: true`.
- Output limits still apply; exceeding them aborts the stream.

## docs/public/adr/0057-server-actions.md

---
adr: 0057
title: "Server actions: form mutations per page with progressive enhancement"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0057: Server Actions — Form Mutations First-Class

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-18

## Context

Forms are the most common mutation path. Requiring a separate API route plus client fetch code
duplicates validation and breaks without JavaScript. Full RPC frameworks add a mental model that
does not fit file routing.

## Decision

1. A page may export `action`, handling `POST` to **the same URL**.
2. `actionSchema` (Standard Schema) validates `FormData` before the action runs; invalid input
   returns `400` with field errors.
3. The action receives `params`, `formData`, `request`, `env`, `log`, `locale`, `json()`, and
   `revalidate()`; it returns `{ message, errors, data, status, headers, redirect }`.
4. Redirects use `303` (POST/Redirect/GET) so refresh does not resubmit.
5. The browser intercepts submissions when JavaScript is available; without JavaScript the form
   performs a normal POST and still works (progressive enhancement).

## Consequences

- Validation lives beside the UI that uses it.
- Actions share the page's loader context (including i18n locale).
- There is no global action router; actions are page-scoped by design.
- Optimistic UI and pending states are the app's responsibility.

## docs/public/adr/0058-edge-target.md

---
adr: 0058
title: "Edge/serverless target: one fetch handler, node:* rejected"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0058: Target Edge/Serverless

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-18

## Context

Platforms like Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy, and serverless functions expose a `fetch(request,
env)` contract. Node APIs (`node:fs`, `node:http`) do not exist there. A separate build with static
imports is required — dynamic file reads cannot work.

## Decision

1. `ramonyx build --target edge` generates a single `dist/edge/index.js` exporting `{ fetch }`.
2. The entry imports pages, API routes, and middleware **statically** (codegen), so no filesystem
   reads happen at runtime.
3. The asset map is inlined; `guardedFetch` moves to a Node-only subpath so the main security entry
   stays edge-safe.
4. The build rejects `node:*` in the edge artifact; the React adapter uses the edge server build.
5. CI runs a **workerd** smoke test of the artifact (SSR, API, actions, env, middleware, 404).

## Consequences

- Same app code, three targets (Node, static, edge).
- Platform bindings arrive per request (`envFromRequest`) and are readable via `env.get/getRaw`.
- Features that need the filesystem at request time are Node-only by design.

## docs/public/adr/0066-revalidate.md

---
adr: 0066
title: "Revalidation: cache loader data, not HTML"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0066: Revalidation (ISR-lite) — Loader Data, Not HTML

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-19

## Context

Caching rendered HTML is tempting (CDN-friendly), but Ramonyx injects per-request CSP nonces into
the document. Caching HTML would serve stale nonces or force per-request cache keys. Data caching
avoids the problem and keeps rendering fresh.

## Decision

1. `revalidate` caches **loader data**, not the HTML document.
2. Cache TTL is `revalidate` seconds; the following equal window serves stale data while refreshing
   in the background (`stale-while-revalidate`), deduplicated per key.
3. Requests with **cookies** or **query strings** bypass the cache (session safety by default).
4. Cache entries carry tags (`cacheTags`, path, route) for on-demand invalidation from loaders or
   actions.
5. The store is pluggable (`KeyValueStore`); the default is in-memory per process.

## Consequences

- Fresh HTML (with a fresh nonce) every request; the expensive part (data) is cached.
- Multi-instance deployments need a shared store to benefit from the cache.
- There is no HTML/CDN purge integration yet.

## docs/public/adr/0069-assets.md

---
adr: 0069
title: "Asset pipeline: manifest + resolver instead of a custom loader"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0069: Asset Pipeline — Manifest + Resolver

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-19

## Context

Node cannot `import photo.png`; only the client bundler can. A custom loader would create two asset
systems and break SSR/edge. Instead, assets need a single source of truth usable by server, client,
and edge output.

## Decision

1. `src/assets/**` is scanned at build time, content-hashed, and copied to the client output.
2. Every asset is recorded in `ramonyx.assets.json` (path → hashed file, bytes, dimensions,
   variants).
3. The server resolves URLs through an `AssetResolver` passed to loaders as `assets`:
   `assets.url(path)` and `assets.image(path)`.
4. `Image` renders the resolved data with anti-CLS dimensions; responsive variants become
   `srcSet` + `<picture>`.
5. Edge builds inline the asset map (no filesystem at runtime).
6. URLs map 1:1 to files under the client output root, so `serveStatic({ prefix: "/assets" })`
   works without special cases. (An earlier layout put files in an `assets/` subdirectory; URLs
   then 404'd for scanned assets. The regression is covered by an HTTP test.)

## Consequences

- One manifest drives SSR, client, edge, and the image plugin.
- Dev serves raw files (no hashes/variants); build output is authoritative.
- Fonts and images share the pipeline; `fontPreloadTag` generates preload links from hashed URLs.

## docs/public/adr/0078-mcp-docs-server.md

---
adr: 0078
title: "MCP docs server: stdio, no hosting, public snapshot"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0078: MCP Docs Server — stdio, No Hosting

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-19

## Context

Agents need structured access to the docs. A hosted MCP server adds hosting, uptime, and
maintenance. The protocol is JSON-RPC over stdio, and the needed surface is small (search, page
read, feature status, rules, ADR index).

## Decision

1. Ship `@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server` (bin `ramonyx-mcp-docs`) running over **stdio** — the client
   launches it locally; there is no hosted service.
2. No external dependencies: a documented subset of JSON-RPC/MCP (initialize, tools, resources,
   ping). Unknown methods return `-32601`.
3. Tools: `search_docs`, `get_page`, `get_feature_status`, `get_rules`, `list_adrs`; resources expose
   the public machine files.
4. The npm package bundles a **snapshot of the public docs** at release time, so `npx` works without
   cloning the repo. The release verifier checks the snapshot and runs a protocol handshake against
   the packed tarball.
5. Reads go through an in-memory index (slug → document); no path traversal from client input.

## Consequences

- Zero hosting cost; the docs version matches the package version.
- Only public documentation is packaged; internal docs are quarantined from the release pipeline.
- HTTP/SSE transport, prompts, sampling, and batching are not supported (documented limitations).

## docs/public/adr/0081-i18n.md

---
adr: 0081
title: "i18n: primitives in core, locale routing in SSR, no auto-detection"
visibility: public
---

# ADR-0081: i18n — Primitives + Locale Routing

- Status: Public summary (the full decision record lives in the internal log)
- Date: 2026-10-19

## Context

A full i18n stack usually means a module or a routing convention. Ramonyx needed routing and
translation helpers without adding dependencies, and without surprising redirects that hurt SEO.

## Decision

1. Edge-safe primitives live in core: `parseAcceptLanguage`, `negotiateLocale`, `localePath`,
   `createTranslator` (interpolation, `Intl.PluralRules`, number/date formatting).
2. `createPageRoutes({ i18n })` registers routes **per locale** with literal prefixes
   (`/id/tentang`), not a dynamic `[locale]` segment — avoiding precedence conflicts with static
   routes and catch-alls.
3. The default locale is unprefixed by default; prefixed default URLs normalize with a `308`.
4. Locale reaches loaders, actions, page props, and the hydration payload; the document gets
   `<html lang>`/`dir` and automatic `hreflang` alternates.
5. Cache keys include the locale, so revalidated pages cannot leak data across languages.
6. No automatic detection/redirect: the helper is available for middleware + cookie flows, which
   keeps behavior explicit and cache-friendly.

## Consequences

- Apps opt in; without `i18n` behavior is unchanged.
- The route table grows linearly with locales.
- No ICU MessageFormat; formatting is `Intl`-based.

## docs/public/api/core-contract.md

# API Reference

The public API surface, grouped by package. Everything is ESM, TypeScript-first, and edge-safe
unless noted.

## `ramonyx` (meta package)

Re-exports the common primitives:

```ts
import {
  route, createHandler, HttpError, defineConfig, resolveConfig,
  createCache, createMemoryStore, mergeHooks, formDataToObject,
  createTranslator, negotiateLocale, localePath, parseAcceptLanguage,
} from "ramonyx";
```

## Server — `@ramonyx/server`

```ts
createHandler(options): FetchHandler
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routes` | `RouteEntry[]` | required |
| `middleware` | `Middleware[]` | `[]` |
| `env` | `EnvReader` | `process.env` |
| `logger` | `Logger` | console |
| `strictValidation` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `hooks` | `AppHooks` | — |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | `1_048_576` |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `10_000` |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | `100` |
| `envFromRequest` | `(request) => EnvReader?` | — |

Also: `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()`, `createMetricsRoute(metrics)`.

## Core — `@ramonyx/core`

```ts
route<Params, Query, Body, Output>({ handler, params?, query?, body?, output? }): RouteDefinition
```

`handler(context)` receives `{ request, params, query, body, env, log, json(), text(), redirect() }`.
Invalid schema input → `400` with `issues`; invalid output → `500`.

Other exports: `HttpError`, `defineConfig`, `resolveConfig`, `mergeHooks`, `formDataToObject`,
`createCache`, `createMemoryStore`, `createTranslator`, `negotiateLocale`, `localePath`,
`parseAcceptLanguage`.

## SSR — `@ramonyx/ssr`

```ts
createPageRoutes({
  pages, renderer, document?, client?, streaming?, hooks?, cache?,
  assets?, i18n?, errorDetails?, maxDocumentBytes?,
}): RouteEntry[]
```

- `client: { script, extraModules? }` enables hydration.
- `i18n: { locales, defaultLocale, prefixDefaultLocale?, directions? }` enables locale routing.
- `document` overrides the HTML shell (`DocumentOptions` includes `title, body, head, scripts,
  status, lang, dir`).

Also: `defaultDocument`, `RAMONYX_MOUNT_ID`, and SEO helpers `sitemapXml`, `robotsTxt`,
`createSeoRoutes`.

## React — `@ramonyx/react`

- `createReactRenderer()` — SSR + streaming renderer.
- `Image` (`@ramonyx/react/assets`) — safe defaults + `<picture>` when variants exist.
- `Link` (`@ramonyx/react/link`) — client navigation + prefetch.
- Types: `PageProps<Data, Params>`, `LayoutProps`, `ErrorPageProps`.

## Compiler — `@ramonyx/compiler`

- `createRouteManifest({ dir, importer? })` — API routes.
- `loadPageRoutes({ dir, apiDir?, importer? })` — page manifest.
- `generateClientEntry(pages, { from })`, `generateServerEntry(options)`,
  `generateRouteTypes(pages)`.
- Loader: `import "@ramonyx/compiler/register"` (TypeScript + JSX for app code).

## Bundler — `@ramonyx/bundler`

- `buildClient(options)`, `buildEdge(options)`, `prerenderRoutes(options)`.
- `readClientScript(clientDir)`, `createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath? })`,
  `assetUrl(manifest, path)`, `readAssetManifest`, `fontPreloadTag`.
- `definePlugin`, `loadPlugins`, `createDevServer`.

## Security — `@ramonyx/security`

`securityHeaders()`, `cspNonce()`, `csrfProtection()`, `rateLimit()`, `parseCookies()`,
`serializeCookie()`, `signValue()`, `verifyValue()`, `createSession()`. The SSRF-guarded fetch is a
Node-only subpath: `import { guardedFetch } from "@ramonyx/security/ssrf"`.

## Adapter runtime — `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime`

`createNodeHost()` (`serve`, `env`), `serveStatic({ dir, prefix, immutable?, headers? })`, and the
in-memory host used by tests. `cacheControl({ maxAge, sMaxAge?, staleWhileRevalidate?, immutable?,
private? })` lives in `@ramonyx/core` (re-exported by `ramonyx`).

## Testing — `@ramonyx/testing`

`createTestServer(options)` / `createTestServerFromHandler(handler)` — in-process requests without
binding a port.

## CLI — `@ramonyx/devtools`

`ramonyx dev | build | start | doctor | version | help`. Build flags: `--static`, `--target edge`,
`--watch`. Dev prints a devtools panel URL (`/__ramonyx/devtools`).

## Diagnostics

Framework errors carry stable `RMX-*` codes. In development, error pages include the stack and
source file; production pages never do.

## docs/public/assets-and-images.md

# Assets & Images

Files in `src/assets/**` are hashed at build time, recorded in a manifest, and resolved through the
server-side asset resolver. Node cannot `import photo.png`, so the resolver is the contract between
SSR and the client bundle.

## Add an asset

```
src/assets/
  logo.svg
  img/hero.png
  fonts/inter.woff2
```

Wire the resolver once in `src/app.ts`:

```ts
import { createAssetResolver } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

const assets = await createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath: true });

createPageRoutes({ pages, renderer, assets /* ... */ });
```

Loaders receive `assets`:

```ts
export async function loader({ assets }) {
  return {
    logo: assets.url("logo.svg"),        // "/assets/logo-3f9a1c2b7d.svg"
    hero: assets.image("img/hero.png"),  // { src, width, height, srcSet?, sources? }
  };
}
```

## Rendering images

`Image` from `@ramonyx/react/assets` supplies safe defaults: explicit dimensions (no layout shift),
`loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, and an optional `<picture>` when responsive variants exist.

```tsx
import { Image } from "@ramonyx/react/assets";

<Image {...data.hero} alt="Hero" sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 640px" />;
```

With the image plugin enabled, `assets.image()` returns `srcSet` and `<source>` entries, so the
markup renders:

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="/assets/img/hero-320-….webp 320w, …" sizes="…" />
  <img src="/assets/img/hero-….png" width="800" height="600" srcset="…" … />
</picture>
```

## Responsive images (build-time variants)

```bash
pnpm add @ramonyx/plugin-image sharp
```

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [imageOptimizer({ widths: [320, 640, 960, 1280], formats: ["webp"] })],
});
```

- Variants are generated at build time (resize + WebP; AVIF is opt-in because it is slower).
- `sharp` is an **optional peer** — installed by the app, not by the framework.
- Results are cached by content hash in `.ramonyx/image-cache`; unchanged images are not re-encoded.
- The original file is always copied and used as the universal fallback.
- Colors/dimensions are recorded in `ramonyx.assets.json` (`width`, `height`, `variants`).

`avif` can be added to `formats` for smaller files at the cost of build time. SVG is passed through
(vector assets do not need variants).

## Fonts

Fonts are hashed like any asset. Preload a font by putting a `<link rel="preload">` tag in page
metadata:

```ts
import { fontPreloadTag } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

export const metadata = {
  title: "Home",
  head: fontPreloadTag("/assets/fonts/inter-6a1b2c3d.woff2"),
};
```

## Honest limitations

- Development serves `src/assets/**` as-is (no hashes, no variants); build output is the source of
  truth for production behavior.
- No blur placeholders (LQIP) or on-demand dev variants yet.
- Image optimization only runs for raster formats (PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF/TIFF).

## docs/public/data-and-caching.md

# Data & Caching

Ramonyx keeps data loading in the page module: a `loader` for reads, an `action` for writes, and an
opt-in cache for expensive work.

## Loaders

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;
export const cacheTags = ["catalog"];

export async function loader({ params }) {
  return { product: await db.products.find(params.id) };
}
```

Loader data is JSON-serializable and available to the component as `data` (and to the client via
the hydration payload).

## Cache semantics

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `revalidate: 60` | Cache loader data for 60 s; the next 60 s serves stale data and refreshes in the background |
| `cacheTags: ["catalog"]` | Tag the entry so `revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] })` removes it |
| no `revalidate` | No caching — loader runs on every request |

Session safety: requests with **cookies** or a **query string** bypass the cache. That keeps
per-user responses out of a shared cache by construction.

The default cache is in-memory (single process). The store interface (`KeyValueStore`) is pluggable
— implement `get/set/delete/invalidateTags` for Redis or another backend and pass it to
`createCache({ store })`. The contract has a shared test suite in the repo.

## On-demand invalidation

```ts
// from an action
await revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] });
```

```ts
// from anywhere with the cache instance
import { createCache } from "ramonyx";
const cache = createCache();
await cache.revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["catalog"] });
```

Invalidation also fires the `onInvalidate` app hook, so observability and plugins can react.

## Server actions

Actions are POST handlers colocated with the page:

```ts
export const actionSchema = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "app",
    validate: (form) => {
      const name = String((form as Record<string, unknown>)?.name ?? "").trim();
      return name.length > 0
        ? { value: { name } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "Name is required", path: ["name"] }] };
    },
  },
};

export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name"));
  await db.customers.create({ name });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["customers"] });
  return { message: `Created ${name}` };
}
```

`actionSchema` validates the form data before the action runs (invalid → `400` + field errors). The
page renders the last action result as `action` (`{ ok, errors?, message?, data? }`). Redirects use
`303` so a refresh does not resubmit.

## Pragmatic notes

- The cache key includes the page path, route params, and (with i18n) the active locale.
- Cached values are process-local; for multi-instance deployments use an external store.
- There is no HTML page cache (CSP nonces make HTML per-request); only **loader data** is cached.
- A CDN can cache the HTML of static/prerendered pages separately.

## docs/public/decisions/frontend-stack.md

# Frontend stack decisions (docs site + landing)

This page records why the public site uses what it uses. Anything not listed here was rejected or
deferred — no silent dependencies.

## Site framework: Ramonyx itself (dogfood)

The public site is `apps/docs`, built with Ramonyx SSR + hydration + soft navigation. It is the
hardest dogfood we have: markdown rendering, search, code blocks, theming, and static export all run
through the framework on every docs deploy.

- **Why**: a documentation site is the first place a framework's rough edges show up. Using it keeps
  the public docs honest.
- **Cost**: features that are trivial in a static-site generator (MDX islands, plugin ecosystem)
  need framework-level work. We accept that cost for now.
- **Alternative rejected**: Next.js + Fumadocs. Faster to assemble, but it would hide exactly the
  regressions the dogfood is meant to catch, and would double the toolchain.

## Styling: hand-written CSS with design tokens (no Tailwind)

The site ships a single stylesheet in the document shell (`createDocument`), built from CSS custom
properties (color, type scale, spacing, radius, motion).

- **Why**: the docs app's client entry is generated from the page graph; wiring a CSS pipeline
  through the generated entry adds build coupling for little benefit at this size. Tokens give full
  control over the retro-terminal/high-contrast look and keep the client bundle CSS-only.
- **Alternative rejected**: Tailwind v4. Good tool, but it would add a build plugin, a content
  scanning step, and class-name churn to a site whose visual system is ~600 lines of CSS.
- **Revisit when**: the site grows beyond ~40 components or needs a component library.

## Animation: CSS transitions + IntersectionObserver

Scroll reveals and hover states use CSS (`prefers-reduced-motion` respected) with one small
IntersectionObserver helper for section reveals.

- **Why**: the landing needs deliberate, sparse motion — not layout animation choreography. CSS
  keeps the bundle ~0 KB for animation.
- **Alternative rejected**: Motion (Framer Motion). ~30 KB for effects we can express in CSS.

## Components: copy-in patterns, not a black-box library

Buttons, tabs, callouts, and the command palette follow shadcn-style copy-in patterns (ownership of
the code), without importing a component package.

## Markdown & code blocks

- `marked` (already used by the docs app) for markdown → HTML. The source is the public docs
  directory (trusted, not user input).
- **Shiki** for syntax highlighting at render time (server only — no highlighter in the client
  bundle), with dual light/dark themes driven by CSS variables.
- Fenced code metadata (` ```ts title="src/app.ts" `) renders a filename bar and a copy button.

## Search: static index + server API

A JSON index is generated from **public** docs only (slug, title, text). The command palette fetches
it once and filters in the browser; the SSR app also exposes `/api/cari` for programmatic search and
tests. Works on the static GitHub Pages export with no search service.

- **Alternative rejected**: Pagefind/Orama. Extra build/service dependency for a 15-page site; the
  index is small enough to filter client-side.

## Theme

Dark by default, light theme via `data-theme="light"`, following `prefers-color-scheme` when the
user has not chosen. The toggle stores the choice in `localStorage`; a tiny nonce-carrying script
applies it before hydration (no layout flash in the common case). Contrast targets WCAG AA.

## Testing

Playwright for navigation, search, code copy, theme toggle, and leak checks (`/docs/adr/0018` must
be 404; internal search queries must return nothing). `axe-core` for accessibility checks.
Lighthouse runs report-only (performance is measured, not gated, until the baselines are stable on
CI hardware).

## docs/public/deployment.md

# Deployment

One app, three targets. The same `src/app.ts` runs on Node, as static files, or as an edge
`fetch` handler.

## Node (default)

```bash
ramonyx build        # client bundle → dist/client (hashed assets + manifest)
ramonyx start        # SSR on the configured port; NODE_ENV=production
```

Set the port/host in `ramonyx.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
export default defineConfig({ server: { port: 3000, host: "0.0.0.0" } });
```

Production notes:

- Serve `dist/client/assets/**` with `immutable` cache headers (the CLI's `start` does this for you).
- The Node adapter compresses responses with brotli/gzip and appends per-chunk for streaming.
- Keep the process behind a reverse proxy for TLS; the runtime verifies TLS for outbound `fetch`.
- Defaults: body 1 MiB, timeout 10 s, concurrency 100. Tune via `createHandler` options.

## Static

```bash
ramonyx build --static     # → dist/static
```

- Static routes are prerendered; dynamic routes need `getStaticPaths`.
- A page with `metadata.status = 404` becomes `404.html`.
- Assets are copied alongside the HTML.
- Deploy the directory to any static host (GitHub Pages, S3, Netlify, …).

## Edge / serverless

```bash
ramonyx build --target edge   # → dist/edge/index.js
```

The artifact exports `{ fetch }` — the standard edge contract:

```js
export const fetch = (request, env) => handler(request);
export default { fetch };
```

- Pages, API routes, actions, middleware, and the asset map are inlined into one bundle.
- Platform bindings (KV, secrets) are forwarded per request: the entry receives `env` and exposes
  it to loaders/actions as `env.get(name)` / `env.getRaw(name)`.
- The build rejects `node:*` imports in the edge artifact (except where shimmed by the platform).
- CI runs a **workerd** smoke test against the edge artifact (Cloudflare's runtime), so SSR, API,
  actions, env bindings, middleware, and 404s are exercised in a real edge runtime.

## Environment variables

| Context | Access |
| --- | --- |
| Node | `env.get("NAME")` (process env by default) |
| Edge | per-request `env` bindings forwarded by the platform adapter |
| Client | never — server values stay server-side |

## Headers & security in production

- `securityHeaders()` + `cspNonce()` from `@ramonyx/security` set CSP (with per-request nonce),
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`.
- HSTS/TLS termination belongs to your proxy or platform.
- Rate limiting and load shedding are in-process by default; use an external store for
  multi-instance deployments.

## docs/public/for-agents.md

# For Agents

Agents get a machine-readable view of Ramonyx that is generated from **public** documentation only:

- [`llms.txt`](https://ramonyxjs.github.io/ramonyx/machine/llms.txt) — index of the public docs and
  machine files.
- [`llms-full.txt`](https://ramonyxjs.github.io/ramonyx/machine/llms-full.txt) — the same content in
  one file.
- `machine/features.json` — feature status, packages, evidence, and honest limitations.
- `machine/rules.json` — rules for writing apps with good/bad examples.
- `machine/adrs.json` — public architecture decisions (one-line decisions + relations).
- `machine/stats.json` — the single source of truth for numbers (version, packages, tests).
- `machine/api.json`, `machine/cli.json`, `machine/config.schema.json` — extracted API/CLI/config
  references.

## MCP server (stdio)

The docs are also available as an MCP server with five tools — `search_docs`, `get_page`,
`get_feature_status`, `get_rules`, `list_adrs`:

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add ramonyx-docs -- npx -y @ramonyx/mcp-docs-server
```

```json
// Cursor: .cursor/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ramonyx-docs": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server"] }
  }
}
```

```json
// OpenCode: opencode.json
{
  "mcp": {
    "ramonyx-docs": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

The server ships a **snapshot of the public docs** at release time, so it works without cloning the
repo. Inside the repository you can point it at the working tree:

```bash
node --import ./tools/register.mjs packages/mcp-docs-server/src/cli.ts --docs docs/public
```

## Ground rules for agents

1. **Facts over guesses.** Feature status comes from `features.json`; numbers from `stats.json`.
2. **Check the limitations field.** Features marked `partial`/`experimental` have documented gaps.
3. **Prefer the public contract.** If something is not in the public docs, do not assume it exists.
4. **Every claim needs evidence.** The machine layer links code/test/ADR paths; follow them.

## docs/public/getting-started.md

# Getting Started

Build a full-stack TypeScript app with file routing, SSR React, and secure defaults. Ramonyx runs
on **Node.js ≥ 24**; the Rust/V8 runtime is experimental.

```bash
pnpm create ramonyx-app my-app
cd my-app
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Vite (5173) → SSR (3000)
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The scaffold ships with a page, an API route, validation, actions,
security middleware, and hydration — all runnable.

## Project layout

```
src/app.ts             createApp() → fetch handler (API + pages + middleware)
src/server.ts          optional custom server entry (CLI still hosts it)
src/routes/            file routing
  page.tsx             route "/"
  layout.tsx           root layout
  [...slug]/page.tsx   404 page (metadata.status = 404)
  middleware.ts        per-folder middleware (root = every route)
  api/halo/[nama].ts   dynamic API route
ramonyx.config.ts      app/server options (optional)
```

## A page with a loader

`src/routes/page.tsx` is an isomorphic module: `loader` runs on the server, the component renders
on the server and then hydrates in the browser.

```tsx
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export const metadata = { title: "Home", description: "My first app" };

export async function loader() {
  return { message: "Hello from the server" };
}

export default function Home({ data }: PageProps<{ message: string }>) {
  return <h1>{data.message}</h1>;
}
```

Loader data must be JSON-serializable (it is embedded in the hydration payload). For
filesystem/database access, use a `*.server.ts` module — the client bundle gets a poison-pill stub
instead of your secrets.

## An API route with validation

`src/routes/api/halo/[nama].ts`:

```ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";
import type { StandardSchema } from "@ramonyx/schema";

const params: StandardSchema<unknown, { nama: string }> = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "my-app",
    validate: (value) =>
      typeof (value as Record<string, unknown>)?.nama === "string"
        ? { value: { nama: (value as { nama: string }).nama } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "nama wajib", path: ["nama"] }] },
  },
};

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  params,
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});
```

Invalid input returns `400` with `issues` before your handler runs.

## A form action

```tsx
export async function action({ formData }: { formData: FormData }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name") ?? "").trim();
  if (name.length === 0) return { errors: { name: "Required" } };
  return { message: `Hello, ${name}!` };
}
```

The runtime re-renders the page with the action result, and the browser intercepts submission so
it works without a page reload — while still working with JavaScript disabled (progressive
enhancement, `POST` + `303` PRG).

## Build & deploy

```bash
ramonyx build             # client bundle → dist/client
ramonyx start             # production SSR (NODE_ENV=production)
ramonyx build --static    # prerender → dist/static (host anywhere)
ramonyx build --target edge   # dist/edge/index.js ({ fetch } contract)
```

See [Deployment](deployment.md) for details, and [Routing](routing.md) /
[SSR & Hydration](ssr-hydration.md) for the runtime model.

## docs/public/plugins.md

# Plugins

A plugin extends an app at build time (Vite), at request time (middleware), through app hooks
(observability/caching), and through the asset pipeline.

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
import { analytics } from "./src/plugins/analytics.ts";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [analytics(), imageOptimizer()],
});
```

`ramonyx dev|build|start` loads plugins from the config. A custom server entry (`src/server.ts`)
still receives their hooks and is wrapped by their middleware — plugins are never duplicated.

## Writing a plugin

```ts
// src/plugins/analytics.ts
import { definePlugin } from "@ramonyx/bundler";
import type { Middleware } from "ramonyx";

const middleware: Middleware = async (context, next) => {
  const started = performance.now();
  const response = await next();
  console.log(context.request.method, new URL(context.request.url).pathname, response.status, Math.round(performance.now() - started));
  return response;
};

export const analytics = () =>
  definePlugin({
    name: "analytics",
    middleware: () => middleware,
    hooks: () => ({
      onLoaderEnd: (event) => {
        /* record loader timing */
      },
    }),
  });
```

| Hook | Runs | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vite` | build/dev | extra Vite plugins (CSS, fonts, aliases) |
| `middleware` | before routing | logging, headers, early blocking |
| `hooks` | request lifecycle | timing, metrics, invalidation |
| `assets` | build, per file | derived outputs (image variants) + dimensions |

`middleware` must be edge-safe (no `node:*`) if you deploy the edge artifact. Middleware runs
**before** application middleware, in plugin order.

## Asset hook

```ts
export const plugin = definePlugin({
  name: "thumbnails",
  async assets(_context, asset) {
    if (!asset.path.endsWith(".png")) return undefined;
    return {
      meta: { width: 800, height: 600 },
      outputs: [{ path: "img/hero-400.webp", data: encoded, width: 400, format: "webp" }],
    };
  },
});
```

Derived files are hashed automatically and recorded as `variants` in the manifest, so
`assets.image()` and `Image` can render them.

## Publishing a plugin

Third-party plugins live in `node_modules`, where Node does **not** strip TypeScript. Ship compiled
JavaScript:

```json
{
  "name": "ramonyx-plugin-analytics",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "default": "./dist/index.js" } },
  "peerDependencies": { "@ramonyx/bundler": "^0.4.0", "ramonyx": "^0.4.0" },
  "engines": { "node": ">=24" }
}
```

- Use `peerDependencies` (not `dependencies`) so types/contracts follow the app's Ramonyx version.
- Heavy dependencies should be **optional peers** (`peerDependenciesMeta`) and imported lazily with
  a clear error — see how `@ramonyx/plugin-image` treats `sharp`.
- Test the hooks directly and in a real app (`ramonyx build|dev|start`).
- Contract stability: the plugin contract becomes **stable** after one release cycle without
  additive changes. Until then it may gain optional hooks (always additive).

## Limitations (honest)

- No plugin registry or `ramonyx add` — install with your package manager.
- No per-route/per-loader plugin hooks (pre-routing middleware + app hooks only).
- Plugin order is config order; there is no explicit priority field.

## docs/public/routing.md

# Routing

Ramonyx maps files under `src/routes/` to URLs. No route config file, no decorators.

```
src/routes/
  page.tsx                 /
  layout.tsx               root layout (wraps every page)
  error.tsx                error boundary for this folder
  [...slug]/page.tsx       catch-all (404 in the template)
  users/
    page.tsx               /users
    [id]/page.tsx          /users/:id
  (marketing)/about/page.tsx   /about        ← route group: parentheses are not in the URL
  api/
    hello.ts               /api/hello
    users/[id].ts          /api/users/:id
```

## Pages

A page module exports:

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | React component receiving `PageProps` |
| `loader` | server-only data loading (GET) |
| `action` | form mutation handler (POST to the same path) |
| `metadata` | title/description/status/robots/canonical/head |
| `revalidate` | cache TTL in seconds (ISR-lite) |
| `cacheTags` | tags for on-demand invalidation |
| `prerender` / `getStaticPaths` | static generation control |

Dynamic segments use `[param]`; catch-all segments use `[...param]`. Route groups `(name)` organize
files without changing URLs. A folder-level `layout.tsx` wraps pages below it; `error.tsx` renders
when a loader/action/render throws an `HttpError` (or any error), with the status preserved.

## Loaders

```ts
export async function loader({ params, query, request, env, log }) {
  const user = await db.user.find(params.id);
  if (user === null) throw new HttpError(404, "User not found");
  return { user };
}
```

The loader context also exposes `assets` (asset resolver) and `locale` (when i18n routing is
enabled). Loader data is embedded in the hydration payload — keep it JSON-serializable.

## API routes

```ts
// src/routes/api/hello/[nama].ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});

export const POST = route({
  handler: async ({ request }) => Response.json({ received: await request.text() }),
});
```

Exported `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` become allowed methods; others return `405` with an
`Allow` header. Query/params/body can be validated with a Standard Schema; invalid input → `400`
with `issues`.

## Middleware

- `src/routes/middleware.ts` runs before every route in that folder (root = every route), in
  root → deepest order. It is edge-safe: no `node:*` imports.
- Application-wide middleware (static files, logging, security headers) is passed to
  `createHandler({ middleware })` in `src/app.ts`.

```ts
export default [
  securityHeaders(),
  cspNonce(),
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),
];
```

## HTTP limits (secure by default)

| Limit | Default | On exceed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request body | 1 MiB | `413` |
| Handler/loader/render | 10 s | `503` + `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 | `503` + `Retry-After` |

Override per app via `createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`.

## Typed routes

`ramonyx build` and `ramonyx dev` generate `.ramonyx/routes.ts` with a typed `routeHref()` helper
and a `RouteParamsMap`, so wrong paths or params fail at type-check time. Import it by relative
path from your app code.

## i18n routing

`createPageRoutes({ i18n: { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" } })` registers a route per
locale (`/id/...`), keeps the default locale unprefixed, sets `<html lang>` + `hreflang`, and
passes `locale` to loaders and page props. See the i18n section in the source docs for the full
guide (translation helper, negotiation, language switcher).

## docs/public/security/overview.md

# Security Overview

Ramonyx is designed to be **secure by default**: limits apply before your code runs, and security
primitives ship in the framework instead of being copy-pasted between apps.

> This page describes mitigations, not guarantees. Security claims without executable tests are not
> made (see the repository's evidence policy). Report vulnerabilities privately via
> [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/RamonyxJS/ramonyx/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Defaults that apply to every app

| Control | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Request body limit | 1 MiB → `413` (checked before routing, including streamed bodies) |
| Handler/loader/render timeout | 10 s → `503`, with `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 → `503` + `Retry-After` (load shedding) |
| SSR document size | 2 MiB → `500` |
| Client bundle boundary | `node:*` imports and `*.server.ts` modules are rejected/stubbed at build time |

All limits are configurable per app (`createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`).

## Security primitives

```ts
import {
  cspNonce,
  csrfProtection,
  rateLimit,
  securityHeaders,
} from "@ramonyx/security";

export default [
  securityHeaders(),        // CSP (with nonce), nosniff, referrer policy, frame-ancestors
  cspNonce(),               // per-request nonce injected into the hydration payload
  csrfProtection(),         // double-submit cookie (Web Crypto HMAC, constant-time compare)
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),  // per client; identity from the adapter
];
```

- **CSP nonce** — the nonce travels with the hydration payload, so inline scripts carry the same
  nonce the policy allows. No `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts.
- **CSRF** — double-submit cookie + header, signed with Web Crypto; compare in constant time.
  `trustProxy` is opt-in, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` cannot evade rate limits by default.
- **Sessions** — cookie parsing/serialization with safe defaults (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure),
  HMAC-signed values, and a small session helper (`read/commit/clear`).
- **Outbound fetch** — `guardedFetch` (from `@ramonyx/security/ssrf`) rejects private/loopback/
  link-local targets, validates every redirect hop, and **pins the resolved IP** so DNS rebinding
  cannot redirect a connection to an internal address.
- **Input validation** — Standard Schema at the trust boundary (params, query, body, form); invalid
  input returns `400` with field-level `issues` before your handler runs.
- **Output safety** — React escaping everywhere; raw HTML requires an explicit
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; server errors never leak stack traces in production.

## Server/client boundary

Server-only code belongs in `*.server.ts` modules. The build:

1. rejects `node:*` imports in page/layout modules (with a message pointing at the file),
2. replaces `*.server.ts` imports in the **client** bundle with a poison-pill stub,
3. scans the client output for leaked Node built-ins.

A secret placed in a plain shared module can still reach the client — keep secrets in
`*.server.ts` or server-only loaders and pass only what the UI needs.

## Runtime (experimental)

The Rust/V8 runtime is experimental. Its permission model is **deny-all by default**
(`--allow-read|write|net|env` opt-in), with worker/process isolation, resource quotas, and an
OS-level sandbox (Landlock) for plugins. It is not part of the production promise yet.

## Dependency & supply chain

- Lockfile committed; `pnpm audit --audit-level high` in CI and weekly.
- New versions must be at least **24 hours old** before adoption (`minimumReleaseAge`), reducing
  exposure to compromised fresh releases.
- npm releases are published from **verified tarballs** with **provenance** (build → verify →
  publish), guarded by tag↔version checks.

## Limitations (honest)

- Rate limiting and load shedding are process-local; multi-instance deployments need a shared
  store.
- CSP is wired through `@ramonyx/security`; if you replace it, you own the policy.
- CSRF protection covers double-submit verification; hidden-field verification for non-JS form
  flows is not implemented.
- The experimental runtime has not had an external security audit.

## docs/public/ssr-hydration.md

# SSR & Hydration

Ramonyx renders pages on the server, sends a hydration payload, and hydrates the same React tree in
the browser. Streaming is opt-in.

## What a request looks like

```
Request → middleware → route match → loader → render (React) → HTML document → Response
```

The document contains:

- the server-rendered markup inside `#ramonyx-root`,
- `<script id="ramonyx-payload">window.__RAMONYX__ = { path, params, data, action, locale }</script>`,
- the hashed client bundle (`/assets/client-<hash>.js`) that hydrates the tree and wires soft
  navigation, prefetch, and form interception.

Because the payload is embedded, there is no extra data request on hydration.

## Streaming (opt-in)

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ app: { streaming: true } });
```

With `streaming: true`, the shell (head + layout) is sent immediately and the body is streamed with
`renderToReadableStream` (edge build of React). Errors after the first byte close the stream — the
status can no longer change. Error pages are always rendered synchronously.

## Layouts & error boundaries

- `layout.tsx` wraps pages in the folder and above; layouts receive `children`.
- `error.tsx` receives `{ error: { status, message, details? } }`. `details` (stack + source file)
  is only included outside production.
- Unknown paths fall through to a catch-all page (the template ships `[...slug]` with
  `metadata.status = 404`).

## Client behavior

| Feature | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Hydration | `hydrateRoot` on the existing markup; no re-render flash |
| Soft navigation | same-origin links fetch the next HTML, swap the container, re-hydrate, `pushState` |
| Prefetch | hover/focus/viewport prefetch with a small LRU cache (8 entries, 30 s TTL, max 2 concurrent) |
| Forms | submit intercepted when JS is available; `POST` + `303` PRG without JS |
| Scroll | `popstate` restores scroll; new navigations start at the top |

## Data loading & caching

Loaders run on the server on every request unless a page opts into caching:

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;                 // seconds (ISR-lite)
export const cacheTags = ["products"];        // for on-demand invalidation

export async function loader() {
  return { products: await db.products.list() };
}
```

- Responses that depend on a session (cookies) or query strings are **not** cached.
- Serve stale data while refreshing in the background (`stale-while-revalidate`).
- Invalidate on demand: `revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["products"] })` from a loader,
  action (`context.revalidate`), or the cache instance.
- The default cache is in-memory per process; the store interface is pluggable for multi-instance
  deployments.

## Server actions

An `action` export turns a page into a mutation endpoint (POST to the same URL). It receives
`{ params, formData, request, env, log, locale, json(), revalidate() }` and can return
`{ message, errors, data, status, headers, redirect }`. A redirect is `303` (POST/Redirect/GET).

```ts
export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  await db.notes.create({ text: String(formData.get("text") ?? "") });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["notes"] });
  return { message: "Saved" };
}
```

## Related primitives

- `AppHooks` (`onRequestStart/End`, `onLoaderEnd`, `onRenderEnd`, `onInvalidate`) for instrumentation.
- `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()` from `@ramonyx/server` for observability.
- Asset resolver + `Image` for hashed assets, responsive images, and anti-CLS dimensions.
